body:
I had a lot of problems separating the video from the audio in the previous container pull requests, maybe there needs to be an abstraction there with audio being the primary sync that the video is snapped to.

However full video playback is a separate problem.

The main thing of note about this commit is that vulkan validation once again reports no issues until we reach `vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR` at which point we segfault somewhere in the driver where my debugger doesn't reach.

VideoStreamH264 takes more responsibility now, it creates the video profile in its entirety, rather than simply adding the little codec specific bit
RenderingDevice now actually has an owner for `VideoProfileState`s and can use it to manage them.
RenderingDeviceCommons has several new enums and structs, which have been mirrored from the Vulkan headers (for now only for VideoProfiles)
And finally by sending VideoProfiles all the way from VideoStreamH264 to RenderingDriverVulkan, it has become far more generic than before, though creating Buffers and Textures still use the hardcoded Profiles rather than being dynamic in any way.

Next step is probably setting up the PDB and active reference pictures. I can't tell why the driver segfaults but I do know that without the PDB and reference pictures we aren't going to decode the stream anyway so might as well.

I have reached the point where we can call `vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR` without either getting a segfault or raising validation warnings.

I have also attempted to *sample* the resulting texture but reached 2 problems
1. `TextureStorage` doesn't recognise the image format `RD::DATA_FORMAT_G8_B8R8_2PLANE_420_UNORM`
2. `vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer` doesn't like using `VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT` to query `VK_FORMAT_G8_B8R8_2PLANE_420_UNORM` images.

They are similar problems with there seemingly being no support for `VK_FORMAT_G8_B8R8_2PLANE_420_UNORM` which just means more work is needed.

Hopefully once the image is finally sampled and rendered to screen it will be mostly ok and implementing rendering entire clusters and eventually the entire video becomes simpler.
Did you decide what codecs? I’m thinking mp4, av1 and vp9

All current work is based on mkv(/webm)/H.264 only.

Of course, it'd be great to separate the "generic" video coding bits from each other so supporting AV1/VP9 is easy but that's still quite a bit away. Also the vulkan headers we use are too old to include VP9 so it might be worth making a PR to update them if you want to support that eventually.

Audio is out of scope of this PR and MP4 definitely is too. Even mkv support is out of scope for implementing vulkan video support but some container was necessary to demux H.264 frames from so that's why it's here.

If you'd like to implement MP4 support based off of this PR I'd be happy to support you in that but the scope is already quite big.
Was thinking vp9, h.264 and av1 on mkv. Not that interested in mp4 container due to our track already doing mkv.

All steps from parsing the mkv file to displaying the first frame should now be completed. The VkCommandBuffer where we stored decode commands is submitted and the resulting image is hopefully copied into the view. Then the view is copied again into a `Ref<Image>` which can finally be displayed.

Unfortunately no frame is actually shown so there is something wrong somewhere in the decoding process which I have yet to find. I suppose there are a lot of other things I could be handling meanwhile like getting all the includes and things under control so the CI builds actually pass and people can test this.

Hopefully, the first frame of whatever video you put it.

Possibly, crashing.

I simply do not know what is wrong here.
I have tried to use samplers and shaders to copy from the ycbcr texture into the rgba texture to no avail.
Vulkan validation is of no help.
And my iGPU doesn't support success queries so I have no idea whether the decode succeded or not and where the problem lies.

I may need a review or who knows because I don't have any more ideas
I feel a little bit better after having compiled the khronos vulkan samples and running my test video on it resulted in a segfault.

Becuase CMake is an absolute mess I ran the wrong file but after running the right one I got something which was.. uh not quite right... but definitely kinda looked like what I was trying to play so at the very least my iGPU supports vulkan video certainly
Are you testing in msvc or mingw? On pc or linux?

Linux desktop (NixOS unstable) my gpu is the igpu in ryzen 9950x

Absolutely no testing has been done on windows

It is now still the case that I haven't managed to decode a Matroska H.264 video with vulkan video APIs.
I've tried enough things that have failed for me to start work on AV1 decoding in the hopes that there may a different result.

I have also updated D3D12 to implement the most recent version of the video decoding API but we'll have to wait to see if there are warnings I need to fix before a Windows build is available from CI.

As for the git history rewrite, since eventually there was going to be a squash anyway, I've rewritten the git history so it's easier to review each step of the decoding (generic vulkan, generic matroska, H.264, AV1) if anyone decides to test this PR.

I am still very much at a loss for why vulkan video is failing to decode which is why progress is slow.

There are still some compiler-specific warnings but thankfully enough succeed for there to be windows/linux artifacts

Windows: https://github.com/ArchercatNEO/godot/actions/runs/18913443158/artifacts/4408251990
Linux: https://github.com/ArchercatNEO/godot/actions/runs/18913443158/artifacts/4408149445

I don't suspect there is much to learn from just starting the editor and importing a video file but if someone knows their way around a GPU profiler maybe there's something useful in memory, who knows.

I am still unsure what exactly I've done that fixed anything but I was finally able to decode the first frame of a video, though it only contains the red channel, I didn't test AV1 but in theory it will work too.
Any idea why the decode has corruption?

Because when I made the video I added a corruption effect. The only real corruption when decoding is that there’s only the red channel (the background should be yellow) but that’s only because when we create the image to display I only used the y component and treated it as a red channel instead of actually converting ycbcr to rgb

This time the image really *is* corrupted (vulkan validation mentions I shouldn't be using `texelFetch` but it was the only one which would do something other than return yellow) but it's in sRGB and was the result of sampling the YUV decoded picture. Sometime I'll get around to making the shader actually do what it's meant to but at least we can be sure the *rest* of the compute pipeline actually works.

Thanks to clay john pointing out that when I was dividing the call index by the texture dimensions using *interger* division instead of float division, the shader can now *finally* ***fully*** decode the very first frame of the video. It's a bit more pixelated than it's meant (I am guessing it is a sampler config issue) to be but otherwise the decoding is correct.

And the first *16* frames looped. I'm not going to do a push yet because it's that's all the functionally I added and would waste CI time for no reason. I should probably get a different video for when I get around to making sure the frames are presented in the correct order but there's certainly *movement* going on.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5da46c3-9275-40f9-9b9c-5772ec463b75

From here there's still a lot to do (getting *all* of the frames decoded would be nice right?) but I think there's still a lot I can do with just these 16 frames. So far I've been leaving garbage around that never gets freed so I think now that we know that if everything is set up right things get decoded it's time to clean up the pipeline.

I'm thinking first of all make `parse frame -> decode frame -> convert frame` into a much smoother timeline which waits on CPU a lot less and making the texture pools actual pools instead of just fixed arrays I keep increasing in size. probably several other things I can't remember right now but yeah *finally* things are happening.

Update on everything: I managed to decode a full H.264 video and decode a small amount of AV1 video ~last Saturday.
The problem was that in video decode order and present order is different, I couldn't manage to rearange the H.264 frames to align with present order so I pivotted back into AV1 decoding. AV1 decoding has significantly more complex state than H.264 which makes maintaining the DPB across the entire video more difficult. It doesn't help that with my driver decoding AV1 wrong can lead to driver crashes which is why I added a crash condition to godot to prevent that happening. There's not currently much point in testing that the crash condition is guaranteed to crash at some point but I though it's been long enough that I should give an update.

If you happen to have an AMD GPU (integrated or dedicated should work) there's a chance you will be able to play H.264 video with frames in the correct order now. If you have an nvidia GPU, chances are nothing will work (check with vulkan validation to confirm). If you have AV1 video, hopefully it plays in order until inevitably the DPB state becomes corrupted and triggers the crash condition (not putting a crash in this situation meant my GPU driver itself crashed so this was preferable for now)

The previous 3 commits were (as the commit messages suggest) just to fix warnings so that CI builds passed.

Not all CI tests pass but sufficient linux and windows builds pass for testing H.264 video, if anyone wants to do so. Mac, Mobile and Web CI fail but since the PR doesn't even have a stable API yet they most likely will not pass for quite some time.

> if anyone wants to do so. Mac, Mobile and Web CI fail but since the PR doesn't even have a stable API yet they most likely will not pass for quite some time 

You can disable Mac, Mobile and Web via python scons

Editor builds are available from the CI at my fork of the repository

In terms of video compatibility, it *might* be possible to decode 10-bit and 12-bit H.264 video now. Additionally, matroska lacing should be supported now (though I haven’t tested). If anyone wants to test the PR I’d be very grateful.

In terms of implementation details, significant amounts of responsibility has been moved into rendering device (which also broke AV1 video) and buffer creation was moved into the codec video stream. I also added support for capability queries which is how 10-bit and 12-bit support was “added” (my GPU doesn’t support either of them for H.264 decoding, I’m assuming that other GPUs might).

Validation of everything is still very much a work in progress but enough should be implemented for me to believe that if your GPU/video combination is unsupported, an error should be logged somewhere. Which means, if anyone has time, finding what GPUs/videos trigger errors could be very helpful for guiding what the next thing I should implement/fix should be.

As for apple, the reason those devices will fail CI (even if I disable the module for mac/ios, which is already done) is that I made API additions to rendering device driver which I haven’t stubbed out in the metal driver which means they will automatically fail CI until I do that.
